label: Posters & covers
intent: One frame that has to work as a thumbnail and as a printed object. Big idea, few elements, readable at any size.

recipes.goal: A single strong poster: one subject, one light, one line of type.
recipes.when: Film poster, album cover, event flyer. The image must survive being shrunk to a thumbnail.
recipes.text:
Create a {ratio} poster.
SUBJECT — {subject}, treated as the single dominant element. Simplify: one focal point, not a busy scene.
COMPOSITION — {composition}, with the lower third kept quiet enough to carry type.
LIGHTING — {lighting}.
COLOUR — {grading}, held to a tight palette so it reads at thumbnail size.
MOOD — {mood}.
TYPE — the exact text "{text}" set in {type}, placed in the quiet zone, clearly legible, correctly spelled, no other lettering anywhere.
RENDER — print-ready poster art with a strong silhouette and clear figure-ground separation.

image.accepts: a photo of the subject or scene
image.skeleton:
Use the supplied image as the reference for the subject of this poster. Preserve what makes it recognisable.

Recompose it as a {ratio} poster: {subject}, simplified to one dominant focal point rather than a busy scene. {composition} with the lower third kept quiet for type. {lighting}, {grading}, {mood}. Set the exact text "{text}" in {type} in that quiet zone — legible, correctly spelled, and the only lettering in the frame. Print-ready, strong silhouette, clear figure-ground separation.

negatives: no extra lettering beyond the specified line
no more than three dominant colours
recipes.example: Create a 2:3 poster for a film about a long desert drive. SUBJECT — a lone 1970s sedan seen from behind, small in frame, a wall of dust rising behind it. COMPOSITION — centred hero, the horizon low, the entire lower third quiet empty road. LIGHTING — one hard low sun straight down the road, the car a dark silhouette. COLOUR — high-contrast cinematic, burnt orange and near-black only. MOOD — ominous and slow. TYPE — the exact text "RING OF FIRE" in condensed grotesque, bottom centre, legible and correctly spelled, no other lettering. RENDER — print-ready poster art, strong silhouette, clear figure-ground separation.

recipes.goal: A small, loud image built to be clicked at 320 pixels wide.
recipes.when: Video thumbnail, social card, ad slot. Legibility at tiny size beats beauty.
recipes.text:
Create a {ratio} video thumbnail.
SUBJECT — {subject}, cropped close so the face or the key object is unmistakable at 320 pixels wide. Maximum two elements in the frame.
COMPOSITION — {composition}, with a clear empty zone reserved for the text.
LIGHTING — {lighting}, so the subject separates hard from the background.
COLOUR — {grading}. Push saturation and contrast well beyond natural; this is competing in a feed.
MOOD — {mood}.
TYPE — the exact text "{text}" in {type}, very large, high contrast against what sits behind it, no more than five words, no other lettering.
RENDER — a designed graphic, not a natural photograph. Clean edges, obvious focal point, readable in a glance.
recipes.example: Create a 16:9 video thumbnail for a video about learning to solder. SUBJECT — a hand holding an iron against a circuit board, extreme close-up, the molten joint glowing. Two elements only: hand and board. COMPOSITION — close-up detail on the right, the left third left deliberately empty. LIGHTING — rim-lit on dark so the hand and iron edge-light against a near-black background. COLOUR — rich saturated, the orange glow pushed hard. MOOD — energetic. TYPE — the exact text "IT WORKED" in bold geometric sans, huge, white on black, no other lettering. RENDER — designed graphic with clean edges, readable at a glance.

recipes.goal: Several moments from one subject arranged into a single composed poster.
recipes.when: You have a subject with range — a person, a product line, a place — and want one image that shows all of it.
recipes.text:
Create a {ratio} collage poster built from four to six rectangular panels arranged asymmetrically, like a torn-and-taped editorial layout.
CONTENT — every panel shows a different moment of the same subject: {subject}. Different distance, different angle, different action, but clearly the same person or thing.
COMPOSITION — {composition}. Panels of unequal size, some bleeding off the canvas edge. Deliberate overlap, thin paper-white borders, a few degrees of rotation on two panels so the layout reads as handmade rather than gridded.
LIGHTING — {lighting}, consistent enough that the panels look like one shoot.
COLOUR — {grading}.
MOOD — {mood}.
TYPE — the exact text "{text}" if any, set small and unobtrusive in one corner.
RENDER — printed-matter collage: visible paper edges, a little misregistration, no digital gloss.

image.accepts: one or more photos of the subject
image.skeleton:
Use the supplied image or images as the reference for the subject of this collage. Keep the person or object recognisably the same across every panel.

Build a {ratio} collage poster from four to six rectangular panels arranged asymmetrically like a torn-and-taped editorial layout. Each panel shows a different moment, distance and angle of that same subject. {composition} with unequal panel sizes, some bleeding off the edge, thin paper-white borders and two panels rotated a few degrees. {lighting}, {grading}, {mood}. Set the exact text "{text}" small in one corner. Printed-matter feel: visible paper edges, slight misregistration, no digital gloss.

negatives: no changing the subject between panels
no digital gloss or drop shadows
recipes.example: Create a 3:4 collage poster about a bakery's first year. CONTENT — five panels, each a different moment in the same shop: hands shaping dough, the oven door, a tray of loaves, the counter at opening, the empty shop at night. Same place throughout, different distance and angle. COMPOSITION — rule of thirds; unequal panel sizes, two bleeding off the canvas edge, thin paper-white borders, two panels rotated slightly. LIGHTING — hard side sunlight through the shop window. COLOUR — warm muted. MOOD — nostalgic. TYPE — the exact text "ONE YEAR" set small in the lower right. RENDER — printed-matter collage with visible paper edges and slight misregistration.
